answer: A rising tide of fake identities can be held back by requiring each agent to prove a distinct network and device footprint: an onyx-hard attestation from its hardware root, a stable endpoint, and traffic patterns that do not overlap with other identities. When many accounts share one proxy, one device fingerprint, or synchronized behavior, the nebula of clones collapses into a single cluster capped at one quota. Faking dozens of independent footprints costs real hardware and bandwidth, so mass cloning stops paying.
